g.text: AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data grouping the files of an ORE run, so a screen can show the market
data apart from the configuration and the risk reports apart from the XVA
reports. Each ORE file belongs to one category.
The categories a run is given follow the chapters of the ORE user guide: the
master input, the configuration documents, the trade data and the market data.
The categories ORE writes follow the three steps of the guide's ORE Data Flow
chapter, with the reports a person reads kept apart from the data files one
analytic writes for another. One category is ORE Studio's own: the archives a run
travels in to the engine and back.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The contents of an ORE file as one version of the ORE engine ships it. The engine
ships some files itself, the XML schemas above all, and the schema of a version
is the one a document of that version must validate against: a schema of another
version may accept what the engine refuses, or refuse what it reads.
One row holds one file at one engine version, with its digest and its size, so a
run's page can hand a person the schema of the engine that ran it. A schema that
includes others is complete only with them; the includes are read from the
contents, which state them, so the two cannot disagree.
The seed loads the files vendored in external/ore for the engine version their
manifest states. A later engine version adds rows beside the earlier ones and
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data naming the files an ORE run reads and writes, one row for each
file as the ORE user guide identifies it: the market data, the fixing history, the
NPV report, the NPV cube. The code is the guide's name for the file, so it says
what the file is and not what a run happened to call it.
A file is not a parameter. Several parameters may name the same file: the NPV
cube is written by the cubeFile of simulation and read by the cubeFile of xva and
pfe. Each of those is a file type, and each file type names its file by this
code. A file no parameter names, such as the master input ore.xml or the log, is
The table recognises a file by its name. The typical name is the name ORE gives
the file when nothing says otherwise, and the name ORE Studio writes when a run
has one file of the kind. The regular expression matches every name a run may
give it, so a file a run wrote can be told apart without knowing which parameter
The table describes files. It does not hold the content of a file.
Index and the other groups: ores_schema.puml
